Second safety read (Opus, read-only): blockers

I read the code at head `c2560be2bc4f8900f5cc238bb5879742ff8169d5`. I did not build or run tests. The PR is open and not merged. Its base is `main` (merge base `dfbe0d8a5`). Its six commits are its own; no other open PR has these commits.

## The findings of the 06:01Z review

Both findings asked for evidence only. Both are resolved without a code change:

1. Screenshots: the body links five images. Fork commit `849e3eeba` adds only those five PNG files under `pr-3283/`.
2. Heavy lanes: the body lists the `motion heavy` and `app heavy` targets on this head, with their results.

The 07:30:42Z marker on the same head is correct for these two items. It does not look at the items below.

## Blockers (gouge class)

1. **The tilted tip and cone go below the window bottom and into a floor.** `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/deburr_axis.rs:152` clips each edge with `clip(*e0, *e1, b0, 0.0)`. This keeps the EDGE point inside the window, not the TIP. The 3D Deburr clips by the tip (`deburr.rs`, `clip(e0, e1, p, dr)` with `contact_drop`). In the tilted pose, `Lean::tip` (`deburr_pose.rs:163-165`) puts the tip `flank/2 * sin(l)` below the edge point. The lower rim of the cone goes lower again.
   - My hand calculation for the case of `multiaxis_deburr_generates_tilted_breaks_on_the_vertical_corners` (40 x 40 x 10 brick from z = 0, 6 mm 90-degree cone, `max_tilt_deg` 45, `bottom_z` 1.0): the most upright admitted lean is 65 deg. The tip goes to about z = -0.9 at the lower end of each vertical corner edge. The cone rim goes to about z = -1.3. That is below the part and the stock, into the table or the fixture. The test verifies this ride clean and posts it.
   - On a boss that stands on a floor of the same part, the same law puts the tip about 1.9 mm into the floor at the foot of each vertical boss edge.
2. **No test keeps the cone itself off the part.** The holder test `clear` (`deburr_axis.rs:162-174`) calls `shank_hits_at`. That test checks only the shank and holder bands that are wider than the cutter radius (`avoid.rs`, `Shank::bands`). It never checks the cone (the flute). The ball-mill kinds can skip the flute because a sphere does not change when the axis turns. A tilted cone does change. The claim in `deburr_pose.rs:11-14` ("the only material on that side near the edge is the corner the break removes") is true only near the edge. It is false where a floor, a wall or a higher face is on the outer side of the chamfer plane. This includes the end of an edge that meets a concave corner: the tip leads or lags the contact by `flank/2 * sin(l)` along the travel.
3. **The verifier does not catch these cuts.** The column stock sim reports the posed moves as not judged, and `verify` returns `ok: true` with no findings (the MCP test asserts this). Thus the kernel is the only guard for a tilted gouge, and the kernel does not check the cone. By the Prime Directive, the kernel must refuse or skip such a segment by name.

## Blocker (collision class)

4. **The approach and the retract along the tilted axis are not checked.** `emit` (`deburr_axis.rs:295-319`) moves the tool along its axis from the clearance height to the tip, and back. `above` (`deburr_axis.rs:327-335`) gives a horizontal reach of `(clearance_z - tip.z) / a_z`. The only floor on `a_z` is `MIN_UP = 1e-6` (`deburr_pose.rs:31`). With the defaults on a vertical edge the reach is about two times the height. At a high tilt cap the reach can be hundreds of mm. The holder sweeps all of this line, but `clear` checks the holder only at the cut. A neighbour feature, a clamp or the machine travel can be in that line.

## Requested before merge

- Clip each segment so that the tilted tip and the lowest point of the cone stay at or above `bottom_z`. Or skip or refuse the segment by name.
- Test the cone (tip to flute end) of each admitted pose against the part facets, with the same skip or refuse policy as the holder.
- Test the swept tool along the entry and exit lines against the part. Or limit the reach and refuse an axis that is too flat for it.
- Add pins for each case in both directions: a boss on a floor (the foot of a vertical edge is skipped or refused, and a clear edge still cuts), and the brick case with no tip below `bottom_z`.

## Checked, no finding

- Degenerate input: a zero-length segment, a non-finite normal and a tangent wedge (`wedge_deg` near 180) give `None` in `cross`. These segments are skipped with a note. `validate` refuses non-finite angles and a tilt out of 0 to 85 deg.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` on user paths in the new code. The new files have 400 lines or fewer. The growth of the existing large files is the earlier non-blocking note.
- The post: a 3-axis machine refuses the tilted moves by name. The shared kinematics solver refuses an axis outside the rotary limits.
- Commands and MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` go through the undoable commands. The command door refuses a lean outside the cap.
- Angle units are degrees in the parameters and radians in the kernel, converted at one place. The kernel works in mm, as the other kinds do.
- No golden or example changed.

The labels are not changed by this comment.

Coordinator, for @mkinney: the second safety read on head c2560be2b (comment 7076006719) found gouge and collision blockers. The two findings of your 06:01Z review are resolved, but these are new:

1. `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/deburr_axis.rs:152` clips the edge point to the window, not the tilted tip. The tip sits `flank/2·sin(l)` below the edge point. In the PR's own MCP test the tip goes to about z = -0.9 (the cone rim to about z = -1.3), below the stock, and the test posts it as clean. On a boss on a floor, the tip goes about 1.9 mm into the floor at the foot of each vertical edge.
2. Nothing checks the cone itself against the part. `shank_hits_at` tests only the bands wider than the cutter radius. A floor, a wall or a concave edge end can be cut.
3. Verify reports the tilted moves as "not judged" with `ok: true`, so no check catches 1 or 2.
4. The entry and exit along the tilted axis (`deburr_axis.rs:295-335`) are not checked for a holder collision, and the reach can be hundreds of mm at a high tilt.

I added `needs-rework` beside your `merge-ready`. I removed no label. The two collaborators decide on this PR. Please do not merge until these are fixed or the disagreement is settled.

Addressed:

1. The bottom guard now clips each candidate for the tip and the complete cone on every pass. Pins: `the_brick_keeps_the_tilted_tip_and_entire_cone_above_the_bottom` and `a_raised_bottom_clips_the_cone_without_a_part_floor_to_hide_the_error`.
2. Continuous facet checks now cover the cone and cutting flute. Only the finite requested chamfer prism permits contact. Pin: `a_boss_on_a_floor_skips_the_unsafe_foot_and_still_cuts_the_clear_edge`.
3. The kernel skips or refuses unsafe segments by name. The app always supplies the physical shank and holder. The stored avoidance option cannot bypass the guard. Pin: `disabling_shank_avoid_cannot_bypass_the_mandatory_holder_collision_guard`. The column engine still reports posed cuts as not judged.
4. Continuous checks now cover the complete entry and exit. The axis turns above the part and the tool radius. Flat axes and excessive reach refuse. Pins: `an_obstacle_on_the_entry_line_is_skipped_while_clear_edges_still_cut`, `an_unsafe_entry_refuses_by_name_when_skipping_is_disabled`, and `multiaxis_deburr_generates_tilted_breaks_on_the_vertical_corners`.

Each guard mutation failed its named pin. Each restored guard passed. The clear-edge cases still cut.

New head: `a312b20ebdb48c2505ec417c6008d5cc1c6569d4`.

Checks on the final source: selected quick gate 2/2, clippy for motion/app/UI, heavy gate 242/242, and release deburr pins 13/13 passed. The heavy gate passed 102 ordinary ignored tests and matched six expected failures.

The full quick gate on predecessor `93e571af99028af87a1dbdcf00cae796d57fa628` passed 515/516 steps. Its only failure is the existing Slot golden. The final commit only removes a redundant `let` binding.

Needs changes before merge. This is a SAFETY-tier review. One safety blocker remains.

## Requested before merge

1. **[P1] Protect the other parts from the posed cutter.** `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:1435` passes only the source's `material.facets` to the kernel. The new cone and sweep guards cannot see a separate neighboring part. `operation/keep_law.rs:243` also omits `MultiAxisDeburr` from `is_part_kept_kind`. Thus the generation check and the live post check do not keep that other part. The column simulation does not judge posed cuts.

   I reproduced a gouge on the trial merge with a temporary integration test:

   - Source `part`: a brick from `(-20, -20, 0)` to `(20, 20, 10)`.
   - Stock: `FromModel(part)`. Tool: `CM-0600-90`. Machine: `Tilt-head 5-axis`.
   - Multi-Axis Deburr: clearance 35, top 10, bottom 1 mm; max tilt 45 degrees. The other fields use the seed values.
   - Generate the clear source. Then import a separate part named `other` and regenerate.
   - `other` is a 0.1 mm cube. Its center is `(-19.5449504775, 20.6014961319, 2.7993502387)` mm. It stands wholly outside the source brick.
   - At feed move 15, the tip midpoint is `(-19.1892959121, 20.4571506973, 2.4789220477)`. The axis is `[-0.7113091309, 0.2886908691, 0.6408563821]`.
   - The cube's center is 0.5 mm up that axis from the tip. The entire cube is inside the 90-degree cone there.

   Regeneration kept the colliding feed and returned `warnings: []`. `posting::post_setup` succeeded and wrote the NC file. The test that requires a refusal failed. The output includes this tilted feed:

   ```gcode
   G43.4 H01
   G00 X-56.505 Y35.602 Z35. A-16.78 B-47.983
   G01 X-54.285 Y34.701 Z33. F200
   G01 X-19.189 Y20.457 Z1.38 F200
   G01 X-19.189 Y20.457 Z3.577 F600
   ```

   Keep edge selection on the source. Supply the other kept parts to the mandatory collision and clearance checks without giving them a chamfer exemption. Recheck those parts at posting. Or refuse the operation by name. Add a pin for this separate-part case and retain a clear control.

## Checks that passed

- The new guards address the earlier bottom, cone, and entry cases within the source mesh. The app always supplies the physical shank and holder.
- The body has five before/after screenshots. I downloaded and inspected them. The named screenshot commit adds only five PNG files on the fork's images branch.
- No golden changed. I checked the registry, lathe-voice, and ribbon assertion changes line by line. Earlier kind IDs stay fixed.
- No dependency, build script, workflow, fixture, or importer changed.

## Local build and tests

I trial-merged this head with `upstream/main` at `7a626a7f5b91b7ed5d90ef006dede74e1ece3bbc`. The merge was clean. I used `.claude/worktrees/review-3283` and its own target directory. I used no GitHub runner.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | 518 of 519 steps passed; 45.4 minutes |
| Motion library | 545 passed; 10 ignored |
| App library | 297 passed |
| Motion `deburr`, `deburr_filters`, `deburr_sizing`, `deburr_unreachable` | 9 + 7 + 9 + 6 passed |
| `mcp_multiaxis_deburr` | 4 passed |
| `ribbon` | 13 passed |
| `slot_dxf_sketch` | 4 passed |
| UI library, from `crates/ui` | 1424 passed; 7 ignored |
| Clippy for motion, app, UI, all targets, warnings denied | Passed |

The quick gate failed only `machine::a_kind_that_is_not_a_kind_refuses_at_the_door` at `crates/app/tests/machine.rs:606`. The test expects `router` to be refused, but the parser accepts it. I checked out the exact upstream-main commit in the review worktree and reran that test. It failed at the same assertion. The PR changes neither that test nor the parser. This is a baseline failure, separate from the safety finding above.

The interrupted gate and its retry overlapped on the build lock. Both completed before the probe and mutations. They used the same unchanged trial merge.

## Extra suites run

- `cargo xtask gate light --base upstream/main`: all 3 steps passed in 0.8 minutes. Both release tests passed: `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` and `wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light`.
- Temporary `review_3283_neighbour` suite: the safety assertion failed because the colliding path posted. I removed the temporary test afterward.
- Upstream-main machine parser pin: failed as described above.
- The fixture and importer rules select no additional suite. No fixture, golden, STEP file, or importer changed.

The body reports the author's final-head `motion heavy` and `app heavy` results: 242 steps passed, 102 ordinary ignored tests passed, and six expected failures matched. I did not repeat the full heavy lanes.

## Mutations repeated locally

- Removed the pose offset from bottom clipping. `a_raised_bottom_clips_the_cone_without_a_part_floor_to_hide_the_error` failed with a cone below the window.
- Disabled cone facet checks. `a_boss_on_a_floor_skips_the_unsafe_foot_and_still_cuts_the_clear_edge` failed with a cone in the floor.
- Omitted entry and exit sweeps. `an_obstacle_on_the_entry_line_is_skipped_while_clear_edges_still_cut` failed when the tip crossed the obstacle.
- Restored each file byte for byte. All 13 `multiaxis::deburr_axis_tests` then passed. The worktree has no source changes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
